title: Collards, frozen, cooked, fat added, NS (fat type 4341)

content.title: About
content.content: Collards are leafy vegetables from the Brassica family. This product is flash‑frozen after cooking and has added vegetable fat to enhance flavor and texture. It is ready to eat after reheating.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Collards are rich in vitamins K, A and C.
They are a staple in Southern U.S. cuisine, often featured in "soul food" dishes.
Freezing shortly after cooking preserves most nutrients.
Added fat improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.
Collards are commonly used in stews, soups, and as a side dish.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K supports blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Vitamins A and C help combat free radicals.

items.title: Improved nutrient absorption
items.content: The added vegetable fat aids the uptake of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: When consumed in moderation, it fits well into calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Allergy to added fats
items.content: Some individuals may react to the vegetable oil used.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The product may contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Texture loss if overheated
items.content: Overcooking can make the leaves soggy and watery.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat the product in a skillet or microwave until hot. Serve as a side to meat, fish, or incorporate into vegetable stews. Add seasonings, garlic, or a squeeze of lemon to boost flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product at –18 °C or lower. After thawing, use within 2–3 days and store in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C.
